programme: SIM1 (hypothalamic energy-balance transcription factor, targets AHR/ARNT2/OXT/EPO), ARX (pancreatic islet alpha-cell identity factor, targets GCG, SST, GHRL, CHGA, SCT, PAX4) and PPARD (peripheral fatty-acid oxidation/glucose-handling nuclear receptor, targets CPT1A, PDK4, FOXO1, SLC2A4, PPARGC1A, INSIG1) trace the hypothalamus-to-islet-to-periphery axis that sets systemic energy balance and the insulin:glucagon ratio.
role_in_a: In pancreatic cancer, tumour-driven islet dysfunction and paraneoplastic new-onset diabetes disrupt the ARX-set insulin:glucagon balance, and PPARD-driven fatty-acid oxidation is a documented feature of the metabolic reprogramming that supports PDAC growth; obesity set by hypothalamic SIM1 signalling is a separately established PDAC risk factor.
role_in_b: In stroke, PPARD-regulated lipid/glucose handling sits on the dyslipidaemia-atherosclerosis pathway to ischaemic risk, and SIM1-linked hypothalamic obesity and the diabetes that follows loss of normal islet insulin:glucagon control (the ARX-dependent axis) are both established, independent drivers of cerebrovascular risk.
shared_axis: Obesity and insulin resistance are independently well-established risk drivers for both pancreatic cancer and ischaemic stroke; SIM1, ARX and PPARD sit at three successive points of the physiological circuit (hypothalamic energy sensing, islet insulin:glucagon setpoint, peripheral fuel handling) whose failure produces that shared metabolic risk state, rather than the two diseases being connected by a documented direct link.
reasoning: The trio names a real, textbook physiological axis and the diabetes/obesity link to both diseases separately is well established in general biomedical knowledge, so this clears 'supported' rather than 'unexpected'. But the retrieved record barely touches it: PPARD's OpenTargets percentiles are unremarkable in both diseases, ARX and SIM1 have no OpenTargets association at all, and the only PMID surfaced is tangential (FTO polymorphisms, not a PPARD-stroke mechanism) — so the connection here rests on outside knowledge, not on what was retrieved.
support: PMID 38161971 — discusses PPARD only in passing alongside FTO variants in a type 2 diabetes/metabolic-disease context; does not establish a PPARD-stroke mechanism directly, so treat as weak, indirect signal only.
how_to_falsify: In PDAC cohorts, compare islet ARX/PAX4 ratio and glucagon output between patients with and without paraneoplastic new-onset diabetes, and in matched ischaemic-stroke cohorts test whether PPARD target expression (PDK4, CPT1A, FOXO1) in blood tracks with insulin-resistance/obesity status rather than with stroke subtype itself. If ARX-linked islet markers are unrelated to diabetes status in PDAC, or PPARD target expression in stroke blood samples is uncorrelated with metabolic-syndrome status, the shared axis does not hold.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (stroke) vs pancreas (cancer), so this can only be a systemic/physiological-axis story, not a local shared-tissue mechanism. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 33 patient-group comparisons, so concordance may partly reflect shared cohort structure rather than independent replication. ARX's retrieved papers are actually about its brain/epilepsy paralog phenotype, not islet biology, and no papers were retrieved for SIM1 relevant to either disease — both are absences in the literature, not evidence against the axis. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed general immune/hematopoietic TFs (STAT2, SPI1, MEF2C, EZH2, LEF1, TAL1, CEBPB, IRF1, E2F2, etc.), so the lack of an inflammatory story here is by design. The record notes no hits at all for any factor in pancreatic cancer under the original search strategy, which is the main reason support is capped at weak.
